title: Frank Stella - Sharpesville, from Multicolored Squares I (Axsom 79) - from the famed Dayton's Gallery (with original label)
medium: Lithograph on J. Green mould-made paper

said.q: At a time when abstract painting is frequently characterized by narrowness of its stylistic range, Stella’s… [art] reveals an extraordinary variety, not simply in the aesthetic structuring of the pictures but in their expressive character
said.in: W. Rubin, Frank Stella, exh. cat., Museum of Modern Art, New York, 1970

said.q: While the catalogue raisonne calls this work "SHARPESVILLE", it is based upon Frank Stella's 1962 original painting called "SHARPEVILLE", and the name of the town in South Africa where the 1960 massacre was committed is also SHARPEVILLE. Deliberately pluralizing the title is a nod to the fact that it is an editioned work, but also the universality of the experience of rioting against injustice.
